case_title: Chhota Ahirwar v. State of Madhya Pradesh
accused_victim_relationship: Relative (the victim is a cousin of the main accused and a relative of the accused); prior land dispute and enmity between the accused and the victim
evidence_type: Eyewitness (injured complainant PW-3 and eyewitness PW-4); medical (PW-8); investigating officer (PW-7); hostile witnesses PW-5, PW-9 and PW-10
confession: None relied on. An alleged confession by the main accused to PW-9 and PW-10 was denied by them and was not relied on
mitigating_circumstances: Accused neither carried arms nor opened fire (not in dispute)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.307/34 IPC; sentenced to five years' rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs.1000
high_court_outcome: Appeal (Criminal Appeal No. 1050 of 1994) dismissed; conviction and sentence upheld
neutral_facts: On 22 October 1992 at about 11 a.m., a quarrel broke out between the accused and the victim over the victim's cultivation of land that the accused had been given for cultivation. The two had a pre-existing land dispute, and the victim was related to a co-accused, who was also related to the accused. The accused stopped the victim on his way to the field and told him not to cultivate the land. The argument grew heated with raised voices, and about 50 to 60 villagers gathered. A co-accused, cycling past, stopped and intervened. The victim told him not to interfere and to go home. The co-accused took a country-made pistol from his trouser pocket, pointed it at the victim, and fired. The victim was struck by splinters on the forehead near his eye, on his lips and on his shoulder, and bled. The victim testified that the accused urged the co-accused to kill him; an eyewitness testified that the accused told the co-accused to beat the victim. A medical officer said the injuries were caused by firearm splinters. After the firing the co-accused fled and the accused followed him. The victim lodged a report at a police chowki, a case was registered, and the investigating officer examined the victim and eyewitnesses and seized blood-stained clothing. Several witnesses did not support the prosecution.
physical_harm: Injuries to forehead near eye, lips and shoulder from pistol splinters, with bleeding; no death
premeditation_planning: No premeditation or prearranged plan found; the main accused's intervention was by chance and any words attributed to the accused were on the spur of the moment
motive: alleged: land dispute and enmity between the accused and the victim over cultivation of land
key_evidence_accepted: PW-5's account that the main accused intervened, took out a pistol and aimed it at the complainant, corroborated by PW-3 and PW-4; the main accused's firing noted as some evidence
witness_credibility: Notable discrepancies between PW-3 and PW-4 on the accused's role raised serious doubts on their accuracy, given enmity and family disputes; PW-5, though hostile, not rejected entirely; PW-3 admitted omitting instigation from his police statement
post_offence_conduct: Prosecution case only: after the firing the main accused fled and the accused followed him; the court made no finding on this
trial_duration: offence: 22 October 1992; trial judgment: 26 August 1994; High Court: 5 November 2008; Supreme Court: 6 February 2020
legal_representation: Accused (appellant): Saurabh Mishra and P. V. Yogeswaran, Advs. State: Rahuk Kaushik, Ms. Bhuvneshwari Pathak, Ms. Shilpi Satyapriya Satyam and Rahul Khatri, Advs.
investigation_status: Report lodged at police chowki; FIR registered as Crime No.110/1992; chargesheet filed; trial with 11 prosecution witnesses completed
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.307/34 IPC. High Court: appeal dismissed. Supreme Court: appeal allowed and accused acquitted
legal_principle_applied: Under s.34 there must be common intention (which may develop at the spot) acting in concert, proved by prearranged plan or facts; mere participation is insufficient; no overt act is needed if the intention is shared
precedent_relied_upon: B.N. Srikantiah v. Siddiah AIR 1958 SC 672; Bharwad Mepa Dana v. State of Bombay AIR 1960 SC 289; Harbans Kaur v. State of Haryana (2005) 9 SCC 195; Manik Das v. State of Assam AIR 2007 SC 2274; Abdul Mannan v. State of Assam (2010) 3 SCC 381; Lallan Rai v. State of Bihar (2003) 1 SCC 268; Ashok Basho (2010) SCC 660; Barendra Kumar Ghosh AIR 1925 PC 1
